front: A diagnosis of schizophrenia requires continuous signs of disturbance persisting for at least {{c1::six months}}, including at least one month of active-phase symptoms.
why: Schizophrenia 6-month duration is DSM detail a passage would supply

front: A major depressive episode requires symptoms to be present nearly every day for at least {{c1::two weeks}}.
why: MDE two-week criterion is a commonly asked discrete on depression

front: Anorexia nervosa requires significantly {{c1::low body weight}}, whereas people with bulimia nervosa are typically of normal weight or overweight.
why: Eating disorders sit outside the 7A category list; weight discriminator is a plausible step

front: Both PTSD and chronic major depression are associated with reduced volume of the {{c1::hippocampus}}.
why: Hippocampal atrophy from cortisol is the standard stress-depression bio link

front: Cluster {{c1::B}} personality disorders are described as dramatic, emotional, or erratic, and include antisocial, borderline, histrionic, and narcissistic personality disorders.
why: Cluster B dramatic/erratic with its four disorders is asked on essentially every exam

front: Generalized anxiety disorder involves excessive, difficult-to-control worry about multiple areas of life occurring more days than not for at least {{c1::six months}}.
why: GAD free-floating worry is the anxiety-disorder definition most often tested

front: How does a manic episode differ from a hypomanic episode?
why: Mania vs hypomania impairment line is the step that decides bipolar I vs II

front: How does OCD differ from obsessive-compulsive personality disorder (OCPD)?
why: OCD vs OCPD ego-dystonic/ego-syntonic contrast is prep-book level; skippable

front: How is schizoaffective disorder distinguished from schizophrenia with mood symptoms?
why: Schizoaffective two-week-without-mood criterion is DSM minutiae beyond the outline

front: In OCD, what is the difference between obsessions and compulsions?
why: Obsession vs compulsion with negative-reinforcement maintenance is core OCD every year

front: Name the major dissociative disorders and their defining features.
why: Dissociative disorders (DID, amnesia/fugue, depersonalization) are named 7A content asked yearly

front: Negative and cognitive symptoms of schizophrenia are associated with reduced dopamine activity in the {{c1::mesocortical}} pathway to the prefrontal cortex.
why: Mesocortical hypoactivity explains negative symptoms; required second half of dopamine hypothesis

front: PTSD is diagnosed only when symptoms persist for more than {{c1::one month}} after trauma; a similar shorter-lasting presentation is called acute stress disorder.
why: PTSD vs acute stress disorder one-month timing is a secondary second step

front: SSRIs treat depression and anxiety by blocking presynaptic reuptake of {{c1::serotonin}}, increasing its availability in the synaptic cleft.
why: SSRI serotonin reuptake blockade is the most-tested bio basis of depression item

front: Systematic desensitization treats phobias by pairing relaxation with gradual exposure to feared stimuli, a counterconditioning technique grounded in {{c1::classical conditioning}}.
why: Systematic desensitization as classical counterconditioning is a common treatment-learning crossover

front: The dopamine hypothesis attributes the positive symptoms of schizophrenia to excess dopamine activity in the {{c1::mesolimbic}} pathway.
why: Dopamine hypothesis mesolimbic excess is tested on essentially every administration

front: Typical antipsychotic drugs reduce positive symptoms of schizophrenia primarily by blocking {{c1::D2 dopamine}} receptors.
why: Antipsychotic D2 blockade is the evidence for the dopamine hypothesis and appears in stems

front: What are the four symptom clusters of PTSD?
why: PTSD four symptom clusters are its defining features on the 7A outline

front: What are the positive symptoms of schizophrenia?
why: Positive vs negative symptoms of schizophrenia is a yearly distinction

front: What are the two core diagnostic domains of autism spectrum disorder?
why: Autism not among the 7A disorder categories; outside section scope

front: What are the two core symptom domains of ADHD, and when must symptoms appear?
why: ADHD not on the 7A outline; age-12 onset rule is DSM trivia

front: What are the two core symptoms of major depressive disorder, at least one of which must be present?
why: Depressed mood/anhedonia core criteria define MDD; asked every year

front: What defines panic disorder beyond simply having panic attacks?
why: Panic disorder = recurrent unexpected attacks plus anticipatory worry; outline definition

front: What distinguishes bipolar I disorder from bipolar II disorder?
why: Bipolar I vs II hinges on mania; a yearly discrete

front: What does the monoamine hypothesis of depression propose?
why: Monoamine hypothesis is the named bio basis of depression tested every year

front: What is a specific phobia, and what is the most effective treatment approach?
why: Specific phobia definition plus exposure treatment; useful but rarely the point

front: What is conversion disorder (functional neurological symptom disorder)?
why: Conversion disorder is the standard somatic symptom exemplar asked as a discrete

front: What is cyclothymic disorder?
why: Cyclothymia is a one-line DSM subtype; two-year criterion is trivia-grade

front: What is persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia)?
why: Dysthymia two-year chronic contrast with MDE is secondary DSM detail

front: What is the core fear in social anxiety disorder?
why: Social anxiety core fear is useful for understanding, rarely asked itself

front: What is the core mechanism of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT)?
why: CBT mechanism is treatment context a passage could use

front: Which personality disorders make up Cluster A, and what is their shared theme?
why: Cluster A odd/eccentric with paranoid/schizoid/schizotypal is asked essentially every year

front: Why are panic attacks frequently mistaken for heart attacks?
why: Clinical flavor restating panic attack symptoms already covered; sympathetic surge lives elsewhere
